_doc: The valley town's people (#756, No Law step 1; docs/missions/BUILD_ORDER.md 0.3): who's in town when, where they stand or sit, and the few props they need, read by ValleyFolk (src/people/valley_folk.gd). A point is `lot` + `at` [a, b]: a metres east of the lot's west side (its x0), b metres back from the street front (north lots: -z, south lots: +z); y the ground's (plus `up`). Each townsman's `day` (townsfolk step 2, #870; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §3): blocks by the hour, each `from` an hour to the next block's (the last runs round to the first), `at` a named spot (`spots`) or `in` a place (on the book: indoors, asleep, out of town), `do` what he does there; a `home` (where he's built and goes when nothing says otherwise). A new person is one entry here. With the clock running into a block (within `walk_in_h`) he walks there by the town's ways (ValleyTown.add_ways plus this file's `places`): out of the last block's door, along, in at the next one's; the clock set past it (a jump, a load at night) and he's there already. Nobody comes out of a door or goes in at one while you can see it (the book's `seen_m`). The night's bar, card table and drinking are in saloon B's bar room (#1230, Sean on #755; till then a stand-in set in the saloon's yard).
status: PROPOSED (#756): who and where are this session's stand-ins; No Law's card (docs/missions/no-law.md) names the barman, the card player and Cody.

set._doc: #1230 (Sean on #755, 2026-11-24: the evening into saloon B): the night's set is saloon B's own (ValleyFolk._bind_hall_set): `hall` the building (its lot), `floor` its ground floor's top in its space; `hall_bar` [x, z] the bar (the kit section nearest: the middle of three, the customers to the west), `hall_table` [x, z] No Law's card table (its spec's `no_law_table`, under the well by the side street's windows) and its four chairs by compass (the building turns them 15 degrees, so near enough), `hall_piano` the bar room's upright and its stool (the building's dressing). `cups` the folk's own tin cups on the table. The yard's stand-in bar, table and piano (from before saloon B was built) are gone; `lot` is the yard's, for the yard's own places (the way round to the outside stair).
set._you_at: Where `--mission=no_law` and the bridge's `walk saloon_room` put you: by the bar facing the card table, off the act's ways (they come in at the corner door and round the room's front).

places._doc: The set's own places, added to the town's ways for the folk: each [a, b] in the set's lot (or in `lot`'s) and what it links to (another of these, or the nearest of the town's places with `nearest`).

In on the door's line to here, 1.6 m in, past their ends, then on.

saloonb_piano._doc: before the piano corner (the upright at [12.4, 12.98]), the fiddler's and the pianist's way

Round the stair's foot by the yard's back.

livery._doc: The livery's door (townsfolk step 3): its lot has no walk, so no door place of its own (ValleyTown); on the dirt before its barn doors.

spots._doc: Named spots (townsfolk brief §3 "Spots"): where a man stands or sits and what he faces, belonging to the place, not the man, so anyone sent there fits. A spot is one of: `behind` a bar (`along` it, + north), `at_bar` (its customers' side), `chair` (the set's card table's, by compass: sat in it by a SitChore), or `lot` + `at` [a, b] (lot_point's) facing `faces` [a, b] (else the street). A day's block names one with `at` (or gives one inline) and says with `do` what he does there (SpotChore, townsfolk step 4, #957): stand, lean, sit, counter, sweep, carry, talk, drink, work, each a loop with its breaks; a spot may give `seat` (a kit prop stood there for `sit`), `tool` (`rug` for sweep: shaken, not swept; `anvil`, `bench` for work), `to` [a, b] (where carry takes the pile), `reach` (how far along sweep goes, m).

book._doc: The book (townsfolk brief §3 "Three ways of being present"): a man indoors or asleep behind a front is a row here, not a body: no cost. A day's block with `in` (a place: a building's door, its lot id, or a way out of town such as `back@0`) puts him on it, doing `do`; he goes in and comes out at that place's door, never while you can see the last step (`seen_m`: past this far off nothing's seen). `doings`: what each shows from the street: `lamp` a lit window while it's `dark` [from, to] by the clock, `smoke` chimney smoke. A building shows them only while someone's in it doing one (BookLights; only buildings, not ways out).

calendar._doc: The town's day kinds (townsfolk brief §3 "The data"): a person's `day` is a list of blocks (every kind) or one list a kind (`ordinary` the default for any kind he hasn't). The town's day runs from `starts_h` to the next (a night's blocks past midnight belong to the day before). Each kind: `week_day` (the town's day number mod 7; day 1 a Monday) or `every` days from `first`, and an optional `if` (StoryState facts, as `talk`'s), the first that holds wins. PROPOSED: Sunday and a fortnight's payday on the Saturday; the story's kinds (mourning, uneasy) go here as `if` entries when the funeral and the news are built. `uneasy` (#1051, PROPOSED): the day after a killing or a shooting the town holds (TownNews sets StoryState news.yesterday at the day's turn; a story act's isn't counted, its day is the story's): the storekeeper keeps in, the loudmouth's out on the walk telling it.

people.name: Sarge

day._doc: #1325: a while at the livery's trough in the afternoon (he sleeps in its loft): the liveryman and he talk mules

people._doc: #1312: the town drunk, Ephraim 'Sarge' Tolliver (docs/story/people.json `town_drunk`; his day is its `day_proposed`): wakes about nine in the livery's loft, sweeps the saloon's walk at ten for the heel-taps, eleven to half past six on the saloon's walk, the store's bench and the jail's walk calling at whoever passes, the hotel's back step for the plate, the bar's door end till half past ten, the loft again. `jibes`: his talk at you is TownDrunk's, not the street's barks. Nerves of steel (Sean, 2026-11-27: `steady`, nerve at its top): he never runs, ducks, cowers or hides, whatever's going on; he carries on and may pass a remark (`react.steady.*`). A stand-in body (the old-timer's) till the Studio makes him; his clothes' colours the card's dust-coloured sack coat.

shops._doc: The town gate's fault 3 (#1167): a shop's open hours and its keeper. A knock at its door while it's open and he's in (on the book at it) brings him out to `spot` facing you, with a line by his regard (TownBarks `knock`, else `pass`, `at` the shop); he goes back to his day once you're `leave_m` off or after `answer_s`. Shut, or him out: nobody comes.

general_store._inside: #1230: in on the book, he comes from here (his counter) at `walk_mps`, `ready_s` to put down what he's at: out at the door that long after the knock, not the instant of it.

shops._1184: #1184: the knock's own line (`knock`) first, then his `pass`; out on his walk within `by_door_m` of the door he answers too; you still within `again_m` `again_s` after his line, he asks again (`knock.wait`).

_no_knock: #1095: places with no door to bang on (PlayerKnock): the saloon (its corner door stands open in its hours; #1230: the night's in its bar room, no longer the open yard). Elsewhere E at a door bangs on it only from outside it (ValleyFolk.past_door).
_doctor_room: #1095: where the doctor has a hurt man laid in his front room when he answers his door to him (FetchHelp.at_door, ValleyFolk.take_in): the doctor's building's own space [x, floor y, z] (config/moments/no_law_carry.json's laid spot, a step back).

dead._doc: The dead taken away (#1051; ValleyFolk._dead_step): a townsman killed in town and seen down (anyone holds it in TownNews), the undertaker comes for him within `seen_h` clock hours; unseen, from `morning_h` the next morning. He walks out to him (at most `walk_at_most_s`), and the body goes once you're `unseen_m` off it or it's out of your view. No Law's Earl keeps his own (`morning`).

regard._doc: How the town treats Harlan (townsfolk step 9, #1152; TownRegard; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §5): each man's trust, fear, liking, respect (DESIGN §9) from 0, nudged by his own news (`view`: his TownNews view of Harlan; `fear_each_more` for each further man he has Harlan shooting) and the story's facts (`facts`: `if` StoryState as `talk`'s, `all` everyone, `who` one man's, `split` the town halves by each man's seed). Band: fear at `afraid_at` afraid; else trust, liking, respect averaged: `warm_at` warm, `cold_at` cold, between wary. What he shows within `show_m` (looked every `look_s`), again once you're `show_clear_m` further off. PROPOSED numbers, to be felt in play.
regard._deeds: What a man saw Harlan do himself (#1167: a shot, a shove, a won pot used to move nothing; #1272: one shove seen turns a man cold, so the room shows it as you pass). Each is what one seen adds; the man it was done to counts it as `to_him` seen; the nth of a kind adds `each_more`^(n-1). `fired`: each of his news versions (seen or told) with Harlan firing and nobody down. Seen: within `see_m` and his Senses see Harlan. PROPOSED numbers.

deeds._drunk: #1312: Sarge's jibes heard (mocked), a nod at one (took_it), a drink stood him, walking him to the jail; the man it's done to counts it as `to_him` (him for the last three). PROPOSED numbers.
deeds._table: #1279, the card table (CardGame.you_did), the table's men whatever they saw: a pot lost is taken in good part; a bluff shown up is a laugh at you (liked, less respected); a raise and a call a little nerve, a fold a little less; sat down sociable, up and off with their money not; a cheat called true is respected and trusted, a false one resented; the man called it his own (caught_him, accused_him).
deeds._bar: #1292, the bar (BarService): the barkeep likes a paying man a little each time (`bought`, his alone); a round stood warms the room (`round`, every man in it); the deputy drinking on duty (`deputy_drinking`, those who see it) and Harlan drunk (`drunk`) cost him respect and trust.

facts._doc: #1312: the drunk, hostile on principle to a badge pinned on by a dying man (his card's `harlan.starts`)
the sheriff brought in well: curious about the man from up the creek; the doctor's respect
he rode by the sheriff: wary to cold
No Law: he sat at the table and never moved (the town split, morning.you_were_there)
stood at the grave: the widow's word carries
No Justice, arrest: the first thing the law's done since the sheriff
No Justice, revenge: the town splits (Sean, #851 pick 3)
he shot the surrendered man: cold from those who work it out (the doctor, the undertaker); a little fear in all
Kett killed in the fight: plain respect and some fear

barks._doc: The barks (townsfolk step 9, TownBarks): the town's script's lines with an `if` (config/town_script.json), the most specific that fits; once a day a person, no line another said within `same_line_s`, one bark at you a group (`group_m`) as you pass (again once you're `group_clear_m` off it). `pools`: each man's pools in the script, his own first (`_default` the rest).
barks._same_line: #1184: was 60; the gate heard one shared line from three men in ten minutes.
barks._group_again: #1184: a group you stand by speaks again after this long (it kept quiet till you'd walked off and back).

chat._doc: Men talking to each other (#1184; ValleyFolk._chat_step): two calm day men within `chat_m` of each other and you within `hear_m` of them; a man once a `gap_s` (give or take `jitter` of it, by his seed and the run's), a pair once a `pair_gap_s`; one says a `chat` line of the town's script (TownBarks, his pools), the other answers a `chat.reply` `reply_s` on. Not a man at play or asleep.
chat._alone_s: #1230: a man sent somewhere to `talk` (an errand round's leg) with nobody there to talk with this long moves on to his next leg; till then he waits, looking about (SpotChore), his mouth still.

overheard._doc: Things to listen to (#1293; Overheard, src/people/overheard.gd): two or three men by each other hold an exchange of the town's script (docs/scripts/town.json, scenes `heard.*`), cast by person and tagged with a place of docs/story/people.json's `places`. It starts with its cast in play, calm, at spots carrying its place (`tags`) and within `talk_m` of each other, you within `start_m`; its `if` asked of the man who opens. Heard whole within `clear_m`, nothing at `hear_m`, `wall` of it with a wall between; the subtitle whole from clarity `full_at`, words dropping out below, nothing under `min_clarity`; it counts as heard (not again that town day) from `heard_at`. A start is looked for once `try_s`, `stagger_s` after another's; each man rests `rest_s` after one (by his seed); the first of a run after `first_s`; lines `pause_s` apart after each is said; `max_at_once` at a time; one not heard may start again after `unheard_again_s`. The card table's are started between hands (CardGame.between_talk), not within `table_gap_s` of the last, the deal waiting `table_hold_s` at most (the talk goes on over the shuffle and the deal). Stopped by a shot within `shot_m`, your shout within `shout_m`, a man of it no longer calm or saying something else. `notice`: you within `m` of one of them for `s` seconds: `chance` he turns to you with a `heard.you` line (not twice in `again_s`). `before_murder`: on No Law's first evening the room talks till the murder's scene begins. `tags`: a spot's own (`spots`), a chair's, a hall's, a lot's (the first tag the nearest; anything else the street). PROPOSED numbers, to be felt in play.

spots._livery_post: #1325: the smith come over to the livery's post brings his shop's talk with him (the smithy is 60 m up the street)

room._doc: The saloon at night as a room (townsfolk step 10, #1157; SaloonRoom, src/people/saloon_room.gd; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §6). Saloon B's bar room (`hall_rect`; #1230, Sean on #755: the night's set, its bar, No Law's card table and the piano corner, are the building's own). **Mood** 0 hushed to 1 roaring, once `every_s`: `people` x (how many are in of `full`) + `drink` x (their drink, 0-1: `drink_per_h` an hour at a drinking spot, `drinks` the doings that count) + `music` while the band sounds + the night's `add` (`nights`: the first whose `if` the story holds, else the day kind's in `kinds`) + Harlan's (`regard`: the town's band of him, only while he's in the room), times how many of the room are calm, times the climb back after trouble (nothing for `hold_s`, then up over `recover_s`). Names: under `hushed_under` hushed; under `calm_at` with trouble not yet lived down or Harlan in and the town cold or afraid: tense; under `lively_at` calm; else lively. **The director** (once `every_s`, only with you within `live_m`): a bit every `gap` seconds by the mood ([mood, least, most] rows, between them by the mood; none under `none_under`), picked by `weight` among `bits` whose `from` (his block's `do`, or `seated`) fits a calm man in the room at his chore who may speak; the same bit from the same man not within `again_s`. laugh: his table (`table_m`) grins, one laughs `second_s` late. toast: glass up and a `room.toast` line (the town's script), the bar lifts theirs. The events: a man coming in is hailed (`room.hail`) and lifts a hand; a man going says `room.leave` and one answers (`room.answer`); you coming in (not again within `enter_again_s`): the town warm, a hail from a warm man who sees you; cold or afraid, the talk drops (`drop`: the mood times `to`, easing back over `s`; mouths shut `quiet_s`; the `looks` nearest look round at you); the barkeep, warm, sets a glass down before you unasked once a night when you've stood `glass.wait_s` within `glass.m` of him (`room.glass`). **The hush** (`trouble`): a deed of `deeds` or a shot within `margin_m` of the room: each man who hasn't sensed it himself (Reaction) looks round `look` = base + per_m x his distance + nerve x his nerve seconds after (0.15 to 1.2), a man with `ducks` (the piano player) ducks instead. `sounds`: stand-ins (SynthSounds) till #807's takes: each one placed at its man. PROPOSED numbers, to be felt in play.

drunk._doc: The town drunk's jibes and answers (TownDrunk, #1312). Within `call_m` and in his sight, one jibe a meeting (a meeting over once you're `gone_m` off for `gone_s`; stood by him `again_s`, another); answered within `answer_s` and `answer_m`; heard by the townsfolk within `hear_m`, one of whom answers `heard_s` on. G at him within `lead_m` walks him to the jail (lost past `lead_lost_m`; in at `jail_in_m` of its door, kept till `jail_until_h`); a glass given him within `give_m`. Sober from waking till `sober_until_h`. Harlan's tags: `run_mps` running, a shot within `shot_near_m` near him, run within `fled_s` of it fled, a blast within `blast_m`. PROPOSED numbers.

talk._doc: What the day folk say when you pass (`says` names a set here): within `near_m` of you, one line each `gap_s` at most, the first entry whose `if` the story holds (StoryState facts: a value, a list of values, "*" set at all, a key with ! not set), its words in turn. Each entry's id is its line in the scripts (docs/scripts/no_law.json, on PR #837's branch till it merges).

You were sat right there at the table, they say. And you never moved.

Sheriff's shot, they say. Laid up at the doc's.

morning._doc: No Law's morning after (#796): once the murder's done (nolaw.murder done) and the clock's in `hours` (it can only get there through the night), nolaw.morning is set. Earl's body, if he's dead, is taken to the undertaker's once you're `unseen_m` off it or it's out of your view: gone from the saloon for good, StoryState nolaw.earl = undertaker and death.earl his record. From `sheriff_from` (the clock) the dying sheriff's scene (SheriffDies, config/moments/sheriff_dies.json) starts, once.
morning.earl_death_doctor: Earl, the card player. Shot by Cody at the saloon's card table, the night after the sheriff was shot; a room full of witnesses, and nobody stopped him. Dead on the way to the doctor's; laid out in his front room overnight, then at the undertaker's.
